justification: The pre-push hook ran the frontend Jest suite even in a bare git worktree with no frontend-nextjs/node_modules, where jest cannot run at all and the push false-fails — forcing --no-verify on every push from a worktree (the project's default workflow). Jest therefore never actually gates in that workflow; it only adds friction. Skip jest when node_modules is absent; it still runs and gates on any push from a full checkout where deps exist. Mirrors the pre-commit TSC fix (#578).

break_it.scenario: A real failing frontend test is pushed from a bare worktree where jest now skips
break_it.what_happens: the failing test would not block that push
break_it.repro: break a jest test and push from a worktree with no node_modules
break_it.how: jest could never run in that context anyway (no deps) so it was already bypassed with --no-verify; the gate still runs fully on any push from a checkout with node_modules, and pytest (which does not need node_modules) still runs on every push

break_it.scenario: node_modules present but broken, so jest errors out
break_it.what_happens: the push would block on a jest error
break_it.how: that is correct fail-closed behaviour for a present-but-broken install (a reinstall problem); the directory-presence check only skips the genuine bare-worktree case

post_merge.secrets: None - no secrets or env vars touched.
post_merge.other_repo: N/A - hook change only; applies via core.hooksPath which existing clones already set.
post_merge.manual_verify: Push from a bare worktree (no frontend-nextjs/node_modules): the hook prints 'Skipped: ... jest cannot run' and proceeds past stage 2 (pytest still runs). Push from a full checkout: jest still runs and blocks on a failing test.
